findings.title: `include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?`, so it is never called
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializer only honours `include_<attr>?` methods. `include_website_name` without the `?` is dead code. As a result `website_name` is always serialized, even when website is blank, and for TL0 users seen by anonymous. It is also not listed in `untrusted_attributes`. The website host leaks for restricted users whose `website` is hidden, and it appears as null when there is no website.

findings.title: `website_name` crashes or misbehaves with blank or unusual website values
findings.body: `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` will return nil for blank values, so `website_name` is nil. For a host-less URI like "example.com" without a scheme, the name is nil and the old client behaviour (split('/')[2]) is lost. If `website_host` is present but `Discourse.current_hostname` is nil (e.g. in some contexts), `discourse_host.split` raises NoMethodError. The URI is parsed repeatedly; compute it once. Also `path` may be a trailing '/', yielding names like 'example.com/'.

findings.title: Sibling-subdomain heuristic is wrong for multi-part TLDs and unrelated domains
findings.body: The check compares host label counts and then everything after the first label. For hosts like `a.co.uk` and `b.co.uk` (same length, > 2 labels), the tails `co.uk` match, so unrelated sites are treated as the same domain and the full path is shown. The comment and the PR title say only 'same domain', but the behaviour is broader than intended.

findings.title: Missing tests for sibling-subdomain branch, blank website and anonymous TL0
findings.body: The tests cover only three of the branches. The `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` branch is untested. So are a website with no path, an invalid or blank website, and a restricted TL0 user (where `website_name` should not be exposed). The TL0 spec's untrusted attribute list does not include `website_name`, which would have exposed the `include_website_name` bug.
